title: Led in groups
hook: the mindful are led to the garden in groups, and greeted with peace (39:73)
tomorrow: Forgiver of sin, accepter of return

segments.voice: Yesterday, don't despair, and your line was never despair of mercy. Did you pick up something you'd let slip? Today ends the week and Surah Az-Zumar. Day five hundred sixty.

Think about how people actually arrive at big places. Nobody walks into a stadium, a wedding, a graduation, entirely alone. They come in clusters: a family, a carload of friends, a team in matching shirts. You can tell who belongs with whom by who they're walking beside. Surah thirty-nine is named for that. Zumar: groups, crowds, companies. And at its very end, it pictures the Day of Judgment not as a long line of individuals, but as people arriving in groups, and the gates they arrive at.

Verse seventy-one: those who denied are driven toward hell in groups, and when they arrive, its gates are opened, and its keepers ask: didn't messengers come to you? Verse seventy-three: those who were mindful of their Lord are led to the garden in groups. When they arrive, and its gates have been opened, its keepers say: salamun 'alaykum, peace be upon you. You've done well, so enter, to stay. Now a small detail that scholars love. In the first verse, when they arrive, its gates are opened, futihat. In the second, there's an extra and: wa futihat, and its gates have been opened. Many commentators read that and as meaning the garden's gates were already open, waiting for them, like a host who unlocks the door before guests reach the house. And look at the first words: peace. Not a test, not a question. A greeting. Then verse seventy-four: the people say, praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us. And the surah ends with the angels circling the Throne, and the words: praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds. Look back across this week and you'll see the same arc: peace on all the messengers; Dawud bowing when he saw his mistake; Ayyub's spring after years of waiting; the sincere that Iblis can't reach; knowledge that leads to night prayer; mercy for those who'd gone too far. And now groups of people, walking together toward open gates, greeted with peace.
screen: `PRAISE TO THE LORD OF THE WORLDS.`

segments.voice: The practice: walk with good people. Sit, and think of the people you spend most of your time with. Picture them as a group walking somewhere together. Which way are they walking? Who makes you kinder, more honest, more patient? Hold one of them in mind and silently thank God, or simply be grateful, for them. Then think of one person you'd like to walk with more often. The bell holds the time.
Led in groups. Az-Zumar's last scene: the mindful led to the garden together, the gates already open, greeted with peace. Today's word.
Your line: greeted with peace. Today, greet the people you walk with first, before they greet you, and mean it. Day five hundred sixty, and the end of the week.

howItsDone: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu 'alaykum, peace be upon you, the same greeting the Qur'an says the angels give at the garden's gates, and are encouraged to keep good company.

original.note: Arabic: in groups, in companies, the word that names surah thirty-nine.

trapdoor: what you thought: on the Day, everyone stands alone.
what it means: Az-Zumar pictures people led in groups, and the garden's gates open with a greeting of peace.
what a scholar hears: 39:71 has futihat, 39:73 wa futihat; many tafsir read the added waw as the gates already open, honoring the arrivals.
